title: HTTP/2 downgrade H2.CL desync to an external script redirect

provenance.disclosure: The decisive /resources + Content-Length: 5 + x=1 shape was seen in an accidentally displayed Solution section. OmniSlash executed, framed, varied and recorded it; it did not invent the gadget.

applies_to.authorization: Only against an in-scope lab or an explicitly authorized target.

preconditions: Front-end negotiates HTTP/2 and downgrades to HTTP/1.1 toward the back-end.
An attacker-controlled exploit server can serve a file at /resources with content type application/javascript and body alert(document.cookie).
The lab victim browser visits the target page and imports the queued response.

response_signals.match: HTTP/2 302 whose Location points to the attacker-controlled exploit host, observed on a request that did not send the smuggled request
response_signals.meaning: The smuggled response was delivered to a different front-end request.

response_signals.match: A victim response body contains the configured success marker
response_signals.meaning: Response-queue poisoning is confirmed by OmniSlash.

negative_signals.meaning: Surplus DATA reached the back-end, but no usable response shift followed.

negative_signals.match: Only 200/404 responses after poison and victim requests
negative_signals.meaning: The desync did not produce a victim-visible queue shift.

evidence.observation: Synthetic victim received 302 with Location to the exploit server /resources/.
Smuggled CL 1 produced no external redirect.
11 poison-only attempts left the queued response for the real browser.
Victim Chrome requested GET /resources/ after the attack.
Full honesty report including accidental solution exposure.

learning.note: Curated prior from one lab instance. It orders candidates only; every run still needs byte-level evidence.
